ability.name: Local Subnet Identification
ability.description: Locate and register the primary CIDR and network interfaces attached to the current target node dynamically.

stages.command_template: $d='C:\Windows\Temp\bas'; if(!(Test-Path $d)){ni -ItemType Directory -Force $d|out-null}; $(try { $ip = Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notlike '127.*' -and $_.PrefixLength -lt 32 } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($ip) { $b = ([System.Net.IPAddress]$ip.IPAddress).GetAddressBytes(); $mk = [System.BitConverter]::GetBytes([uint32]([Math]::Pow(2,32)-[Math]::Pow(2,32-$ip.PrefixLength))); if ([BitConverter]::IsLittleEndian) { [Array]::Reverse($mk) }; $net = (0..3|ForEach-Object{$b[$_]-band $mk[$_]}) -join '.'; $cidr = "$net/$($ip.PrefixLength)"; Write-Output "NETWORK_CIDR: $cidr"; $cidr | Out-File C:\Windows\Temp\bas\network_cidr.txt -Encoding ascii } else { throw "No active IPv4 adapters found" } } catch { Write-Output "ERROR: step1 $($_.Exception.Message)" }) | Tee-Object -FilePath $d\network_cidr_out.txt

rationale: Determining the local subnet configuration dynamically is a mandatory step before any active scanning or host sweeps can be executed securely.
